text: um please pray for Brother [[Ray]] he goes in for the heart cath on Tuesday and his wife [[Delphine]] is just worn out
we lift up little [[Josiah Pruitt]] he's four years old and he's been in Children's Hospital since Sunday with pneumonia and lord we just ask that you would breathe on those little lungs
pray for [[Naomi]] y'all. She lost her husband in March and like {{Naomi}} in the book of {{Ruth}} she says call me bitter. Lord fill her back up.
and pray for the [[Okonkwos]], they land in Lagos on Thursday to bury [[Chidi]]'s father
Mr. [[Vasquez]] is having his hip replaced Friday morning so if you see him please don't hug him too hard
can y'all pray for my coworker [[Tanya]] she's going through a divorce and she doesn't know the Lord yet, amen [[Danny]]? Amen.
Sister [[Grace]] is in room 214 and she'd love some visitors. And I mean [[Grace]] the person, not grace the doctrine, although she'd take both.
pray for [[Precious]] she takes her nursing boards tomorrow and she has not slept
Lord put [[Esther]] in the right place at the right time like you did for Queen {{Esther}}, she's interviewing at the county office Monday
pray for my uncle [[Ahmad]] and his family in Dearborn, his brother [[Yusuf]] is still missing after the flood and they don't know anything
keep praying for Pastor [[Wendell]] over at Mt. Zion he had that stroke two weeks ago and his church is hurting
please pray for [[brooke]] and her husband [[caleb]] they are expecting twins and she's on bedrest
we are praying for Mrs. [[Oakley]] who turned ninety-one and fell again in the kitchen, she says she's fine, she is not fine
pray for the president and for the country, and pray for President {{Carter}}'s family and the whole town of Plains
my son [[Mateo]] starts radiation next week and we are scared, and his wife [[Luz]] is carrying all of it, so Lord we need you
Pray for [[Hope]]. Not hope in general, though we all need that, I mean [[Hope Delgado]] from the praise team, her surgery is tomorrow at seven.
Father we ask for [[Gabriel]]'s healing the way you healed the man at the pool of Bethesda, he's been down thirty-eight days, not years, but it feels like years
please remember [[Svetlana]] and [[Dmitri]] and their kids whose family is still in Kharkiv and cannot get through on the phone
Mrs. [[Tran]] lost her husband [[Minh]] last week and the viewing is Friday night at the funeral home on Main, so bring a dish to the house
pray for [[Seth]] he has a deposition in the morning and he's been up all night
pray for Coach [[Danny]] at the high school, they lost in the playoffs and he's taking it hard
Father be with [[Rebecca]] as she drives her mother to Duke every week, give her strength for the road and for the waiting room
we pray for the [[Wangs]], [[Li Wei]] lost his job at the plant and they have a mortgage and two in college
pray for sister [[Rosa]] and her mother in Oaxaca who has not been well and also for brother [[Efrain]] who is out of work and doesn't say anything but we know
Lord {{Jesus}} we ask you to give joy to [[Joy]] who has stage three and doesn't have much joy right now. You are the joy giver.
please pray for [[Ezra]] he's sixteen and hasn't been to youth group in months and his mom [[Charlene]] is heartbroken
Lord {{Jesus}} hold [[Marcus]] in his grief he buried his brother Saturday
can we pray for [[Blessing]]? She's our nursery volunteer and her mom in Abuja passed this morning. Pray she can get a flight.
pray for the [[Hendersons]] who are closing on the house, and for Ms. [[Patrice]] at the bank who has been so kind to them
pray for the [[Castellanos]] family, [[Elias]] and [[Mary]], their oldest is leaving for the Marines in June
pray for [[Chance]] he's got a tryout and he's nervous, I told him you've got a chance, but it's up to God
pray for Sister [[Dolores]]'s granddaughter [[Aaliyah]] who is sixteen and made some choices
and our missionaries the [[Pattersons]] in Mozambique, pray their visas come through
Lord you fed the widow of Zarephath with a jar of flour and a little oil when you sent {{Elijah}} to her door, and we ask the same for Miss [[Bernice]] whose power just got cut off
pray for Deacon [[Hollis]] and for all our deacons, we ask that you would knit them together
pray for josh and amber and baby noah they are home from the NICU finally
pray for my boss Mr. [[Feldman]] he doesn't know God but he asked me yesterday why I'm so calm
and Lord we lift up [[Mercy]] and her sisters, may your mercy find them right where they are
pray for [[Fatima]] and her little brother [[Omar]], their dad is in the hospital in Amman and they can't get there
{{Hosea}} took back a wife who left him, and I think about [[Tyrone]] who is trying to do the same. Pray for [[Tyrone]] and [[Keisha]]. They have a counselor appointment Thursday.
Mrs. [[Alderman]] has been sick twelve years, same as that woman in {{Mark}} five who touched the hem of his garment. Touch her, Lord. Amen.
Pray for Pastor [[Samuel]] and his church in Port-au-Prince. {{Samuel}} heard the voice in the night and said speak, your servant is listening, and we pray he hears you too.
My neighbor [[Mohamed]] lost his shop in the fire. He's not a believer but he said thank you when we prayed. Pray for [[Mohamed]] and his boys [[Idris]] and [[Bilal]].
prayers for the [[Nowaks]], their daughter [[Magda]] is in surgery in Krakow and they're on the phone all night. Lord be near them like you were to {{Paul}} in prison.
Pray for [[Faith]]. Not faith, I know we all pray for more faith, but [[Faith Lindgren]] who works the tech desk, and whose husband [[Per]] is deployed overseas.
Ms. [[Okoye]] teaches third grade and asked us to pray for her class. Pray also for the bus driver, Mr. [[Delgado]], who has a new baby and no sleep.
so men's breakfast is Saturday at seven thirty, [[Walt]] is cooking his famous biscuits so come hungry, and bring a friend
VBS volunteers we still need two more in the craft room, see Mrs. [[Delacroix]] after service or just find [[Kimberly]] in the lobby
the Wednesday night meal is spaghetti and thank you to [[Rodney]] and [[Pat]] for the sauce, it is amazing
we are collecting the {{Lottie Moon}} offering through December, and [[Barb]] has the envelopes at the welcome table
youth are going to Camp Riverbend in July and Pastor [[Josh]] needs the permission slips by Friday, no slip no bus
baby shower for [[Yesenia]] is next Sunday after church in the fellowship hall, she's registered at Target and she is having a girl so expect lots of pink
reminder the church office is closed Monday for the holiday, if it's an emergency call Pastor [[Alvin]] on his cell
Hey, the parking lot team needs help, [[Terrence]] hurt his back and we need someone to cover the east lot. Talk to [[Terrence]] if you want the orange vest.
we want to welcome the new family in the back, I'm sorry sir I didn't catch your name, [[Obinna]] right, and his wife [[Ngozi]] and their three boys, welcome, stand up boys
choir rehearsal moves to six o'clock Thursday because Ms. [[Vernita]] has a doctor's appointment and [[Cassie]] will be directing
We're showing the new documentary on {{Billy Graham}} Friday night in the fellowship hall and [[Hank]] is bringing the projector. Popcorn is free, popcorn is always free.
Our adult Sunday school is studying 2 {{Timothy}} this quarter, [[Gil]] teaches the Sunday class and [[Joanne]] has the Wednesday group
the food pantry served 212 families last month, praise God, and a special thank you to [[Esperanza]] and her crew who sort every Tuesday
sign up for the church picnic, bring a side dish, last names A through M bring desserts, [[Melvin]] has the clipboard
i want to remind everybody that tamika is taking the baby dedication forms so please see her after the service
funeral for Mr. [[Abernathy]] will be Thursday at eleven, family will receive friends at ten, and the ladies are doing the meal
Congratulations to [[Jasmine]] and [[Darnell]] on their engagement. He asked her on the roof of the fellowship hall, I'm not kidding, and [[Jasmine]] said yes before he got down.
This week in the nursery we need volunteers, and Sister [[Blessing]] has been there faithfully since January so let's give her a hand
the new members class starts at nine, [[Paula]] and I will be teaching it, we'll cover what we believe, who {{Jesus}} is, and how to get plugged in
Next Sunday is Pentecost, wear red, and the choir will sing, and [[Isaiah Bellamy]] will be on trumpet, that's right, our own
We have a Hispanic ministry service at one, Pastor [[Ruben]] preaching, and everybody's welcome, y todos son bienvenidos
the sound booth needs somebody, [[Cody]] is leaving for college and the rest of us think the board is a mystery
Mother's Day we'll give a rose to the oldest mom, last year was Mrs. [[Fontenot]] at ninety-six, who's got it this year
mission trip to Honduras is full, thank you for signing up, [[Lupe]] has the packing list and [[Frank]] has the vaccine info
Reformation Day is October thirty-first, come dressed as {{Martin Luther}} or {{John Calvin}} or just a regular sinner, and [[Trish]] is doing the chili
prayer chain, if you need to be added call [[Eunice]] at the office, she keeps the list
huge thanks to the [[Whitfields]] for hosting small group last night, and [[Dale]], man, your chili
Wednesday Bible study is in the Gospel of {{Luke}}, we're in {{Luke}} 15 this week, the prodigal son, bring your questions, and [[Marisol]] is bringing coffee
there's a new baby, [[Hadassah Grace]] arrived Tuesday, seven pounds, and [[Aaron]] and [[Leah]] are doing great
the elders are meeting after service, that's [[Roger]], [[Bill]], [[Sam]] and [[Mike]], please don't skip lunch
turn in your Angel Tree gifts by the fifteenth, that's the prison ministry that {{Chuck Colson}} started, and [[Wanda]] will take them downstairs
The ladies' tea is Saturday, tickets are ten dollars, see [[Yolanda]] or Mrs. [[Pickett]]
Sunday school teachers please pick up your curriculum from [[Neil]] who is sitting right there waving, hi [[Neil]]
We are collecting blankets for the shelter, and thanks to the [[Gonzalez]] family for the forty they donated
Scoutmaster [[Dwayne]] says the camp-out is still on even if it rains, bring a tarp
the car wash is saturday at the church lot and kevin and little ty are in charge of the hoses
Pastor [[Gene]] and his wife [[Ruth]] are in Charlotte this week at the {{Billy Graham}} Library for a pastors' retreat, so no evening service tonight
Our guest next Sunday is a missionary from Kenya, Dr. [[Wanjiru Kamau]], and she'll be speaking at both services and then we're taking her to lunch
Next Sunday we baptize four people. [[Rose]] is one of them, and [[Will]] and his brother [[Mason]] and little [[Kiara]]. Bring a towel, because last time the carpet was ruined.
Pastor [[Don]] is out this week, so [[Kyle]] will preach on {{Philemon}}. Yes, {{Philemon}}, it's one chapter, you can handle it.
The Easter egg hunt is the Saturday before. [[Priscilla]] is hiding the eggs. Bring a basket, bring your cousins.
Somebody left a jacket with {{Dale Earnhardt}} on the back in the nursery. If it's yours see [[Maureen]]. If it isn't yours please put it back.
The Lord's Supper is first Sunday. [[Hank]] and [[Orlando]] are serving. Remember {{Paul}} says in 1 Corinthians to examine yourselves.
Revival starts Monday night with Evangelist [[Marcellus Reed]]. Seven o'clock. Childcare is by [[Lakeisha]], so no excuses.
Thanksgiving baskets, we need turkeys. Sister [[Odalys]] and her husband [[Reinaldo]] will pick them up. Last year we gave out ninety baskets, let's do a hundred.
so I was sitting in the truck in the parking lot at Lowe's and I was done, I mean done, and my buddy [[Travis]] calls me out of nowhere and says I just feel like I need to pray with you
my mother [[Concepcion]] raised four of us by herself cleaning offices at night and she never once missed church, and when she passed I found her Bible with all our names written in the margins
I was a prodigal, y'all, I'm the one in {{Luke}} 15, I took my daddy's money and I went to Myrtle Beach and I came home with nothing. And my daddy [[Harlan]] ran out to the road.
Miss [[Pearl]] from the nursing home told me every Tuesday, baby, the Lord is not done with you, and I didn't believe her for two years
When my husband [[Raul]] got laid off I said God where are you, and then Sister [[Inez]] left a bag of groceries on the porch with no note, and I knew
I got saved at fifteen at a revival under a tent, a preacher named Brother [[Cleophus]], and I still remember the sawdust on the floor
I'm not good at talking up here but my wife [[Abigail]] said I had to so here goes
and I read {{Job}} for the first time that winter, the whole thing, and it was the first book that did not lie to me
I was in the Army, deployed, and my sergeant [[Okafor]] would pray before every patrol, and I laughed at him, and then one night in Kandahar I didn't

when my daughter [[Joy]] was born at twenty-six weeks the doctors said, and I'm quoting, prepare yourselves, and we named her [[Joy]] because we needed some, and today she's eleven and she's here in the second row waving
The thing that changed me was a sermon by Dr. {{Tony Evans}} on the radio, I was driving a truck outside Memphis and I had to pull over
my brother [[Jerome]] and I did not speak for eleven years over our daddy's land, and then at the funeral he just put his arm around me
I got sober November 3rd, two thousand and nineteen, and I want to thank my sponsor [[Lonnie]] and this church for not giving up on me

I was raised Catholic in Guadalajara, my abuela [[Socorro]] prayed the rosary every night, and when I came to this country and found an evangelical church I thought I was betraying her, but she was the one who showed me {{Jesus}}
my best friend rachel and her husband jonah brought me meals for three months after the surgery and never once made me feel like a burden
My name is [[Will]] and for thirty years I lived up to it, whatever my will was, I did it, and then God broke my will, and he did it gently
I lost my job at the mill after twenty-two years, the foreman [[Gary]] called me in at seven in the morning and I knew by his face

My son [[Elijah]] is seventeen and he told me last spring he didn't believe any of it. And I thought about {{Elijah}} under the broom tree saying take my life, and how God sent him bread. For me the bread was a youth leader named [[Marcus]].
We came from Lebanon in ninety-two, and my father [[Georges]] said we would only survive if we found a church that would feed us, and it was the Presbyterians on Elm Street who did
My cousin [[Destiny]] always said everybody has a destiny and I rolled my eyes, and then she got sick and showed me hers
I'm just a regular guy. My granddaddy [[Otis]] took me fishing every Saturday and said the same thing, son, you can't catch nothing in your sleep.
When the tornado came through we hid in the closet, me and [[Tasha]] and the baby, and Pastor [[Mike]] called before the sirens even stopped
the doctor said it's a miracle and I said no it's the prayers of this church. That's why we call our daughter [[Miracle]], and she's right there, wave baby.
three years ago I walked into this building drunk at ten in the morning looking for the bathroom and [[Frances]] at the front desk didn't call the cops, she called Pastor [[Greg]]
I read {{Augustine}}'s Confessions in prison, a chaplain, Mr. [[Beasley]], gave it to me, and when I got to restless until it rests in thee I just cried
I grew up in Seoul and my grandmother [[Kim Sook-ja]] walked every morning to the prayer mountain before the sun came up
After my stroke I couldn't say my own wife's name, [[Loretta]], but I could say {{Jesus}}. Isn't that something. I couldn't say [[Loretta]] but I could say {{Jesus}}.
my testimony is short, I used to cuss, now I don't, ask [[Delbert]]
my cousin handed me a {{Lecrae}} CD when I was nineteen and I played it till it skipped, and that's where I first heard the gospel in a language I understood
every time I wanted to quit nursing school [[Adaeze]] texted me a verse, and I'm telling you she never missed a week
We were homeless eight months, living in a Kia with [[Jayden]] and [[Kaylee]], and the church paid for a motel when it got cold
I wanted to run like {{Jonah}} so I ran, I got on a Greyhound, and the bus broke down in Atlanta, and the driver, Mr. [[Pettigrew]], looked at me and said son, where you running to?
and my little girl [[Ruby]] asked why the lady at the grocery store was crying, so we went back and prayed with her, and that's the day [[Ruby]] led her first person to the Lord
Pastor [[Terry]] visited me in the hospital every day, twenty-three days, and he never said a word about my choices, he just brought me pudding

I came from a Muslim family in Dearborn, my father [[Tariq]] said never go in a church, and then my coworker [[Sandra]] invited me to a Christmas Eve candlelight and later I read about {{Jesus}} in the Gospel of {{John}}
My first wife [[Colleen]] left and I thought God left too. And then I read {{Job}} thirty-eight, where God answers out of the whirlwind, and I just sat on the bathroom floor and cried.
My mama [[Dorothea]] used to hum {{Mahalia Jackson}} while she ironed, and I didn't know what the words meant until I was forty
I'll be honest with y'all, i wasnt sure about this church, the first time i came [[Hector]] shook my hand so hard I thought he was going to break it

I was an atheist in college, reading {{Richard Dawkins}} and {{Christopher Hitchens}} for fun. Then my roommate [[Aaron]] asked me one question I couldn't answer. I read {{C. S. Lewis}} to prove him wrong and lost.
In 2008 I lost the house. My wife [[Marlene]] and I sat in the car and sang Blessed Assurance, which {{Fanny Crosby}} wrote, and we didn't know if we'd eat, but we sang.
My little sister [[Hannah]] has Down syndrome and she prays better than I do. Like {{Hannah}} in the temple she's not ashamed to ask. She asked for a bicycle and Saturday she got one.

When I was in Nairobi a pastor named [[Joseph Mwangi]] fed forty kids out of his own house. I came back and couldn't look at my pantry the same. {{Jesus}} said whatever you did for the least of these.

My dad [[Walter]] was a hard man. At his funeral the preacher read the story of {{Joseph}} forgiving his brothers, you meant it for evil but God meant it for good, and I forgave him right there in the pew.

I'm a nurse, and one night Mr. [[Yoon]], an old Korean man, held my hand and asked me to pray for him in English because he said God understands every language but he wanted to hear it. I said the Lord's Prayer. He said amen.

My boy [[Gabriel]] was named for the angel, and he is a handful, not an angel. But when he got his first guitar he started writing songs for {{Jesus}}, and last week he played one for Mrs. [[Pruitt]] at the nursing home.
so {{Moses}} is out in the wilderness with the sheep, forty years now, and he sees this bush that's burning and not burning up
and {{Jesus}} turns to {{Peter}} and says who do you say that I am, and {{Peter}} gets it right for once

{{Mary}} and {{Martha}} are both in the house, and {{Martha}} is in the kitchen banging pots, and {{Mary}} is just sitting there at the feet of {{Jesus}}. And you know that's [[Brenda]] and [[Colette]] every Wednesday night.
{{Joseph}} gets thrown in the pit by his own brothers, {{Reuben}} and {{Judah}} and the rest, and sold for twenty pieces of silver
so {{David}} walks onto the field with five smooth stones and {{Goliath}} laughs and then he doesn't
{{Paul}} writes to {{Timothy}} his son in the faith and says don't let anyone despise your youth
{{Ruth}} says to {{Naomi}} where you go I will go, and that is not a wedding verse, people, that's a mother-in-law verse
and the angel {{Gabriel}} appears to {{Mary}} and says do not be afraid you have found favor, and she says how can this be
{{Hannah}} is weeping in the temple and old {{Eli}} thinks she's drunk, which, I mean, we've all been misread at the altar
{{Jonah}} gets on a boat headed to Tarshish, which is the opposite direction from Nineveh, and God sends a storm, a great fish, and a second chance
{{Esther}} goes before the king without being called, and {{Mordecai}} had told her who knows if you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this
in the Gospel of {{John}} chapter eleven, {{Jesus}} weeps, shortest verse in the Bible, standing at the tomb of {{Lazarus}} while {{Martha}} is saying Lord if you had been here
so {{Daniel}} gets the news that the king has signed the decree, and he goes home, opens his windows toward Jerusalem, and prays three times a day just like before
{{Zacchaeus}} was a short man and he climbs up a sycamore tree. And you know if he went to our church somebody would have gotten him a chair.
{{Abraham}} is a hundred years old and {{Sarah}} is ninety and God says you'll have a son. And {{Sarah}} laughs. And I don't blame her.
and then {{Stephen}} is being stoned and standing there holding the coats is a young man named {{Saul}}, who later becomes {{Paul}}
{{Rahab}}, a woman of Jericho, hides the spies on her roof, and she ends up in the line of {{Jesus}}, right there in {{Matthew}} chapter one
in Acts 9 {{Ananias}} gets a vision and God says go to Straight Street and find {{Saul}}, and {{Ananias}} says Lord have you heard what this man has done

{{Elijah}} sat under the broom tree and said I've had enough, Lord. That's what [[Gordon]] told me after the layoffs, almost word for word. And God didn't give {{Elijah}} a sermon, he gave him a nap and some bread.
and then jesus says to the disciples let's go to the other side and the storm comes up and jesus is asleep in the back of the boat on a cushion
{{Mary Magdalene}} goes to the tomb while it is still dark, early on the first day of the week, and she sees the stone rolled away
So {{Nicodemus}} comes at night. Why at night? Because he's got a reputation, he's a ruler of the Jews, and he can't be seen with {{Jesus}}.
{{Joshua}} and {{Caleb}} come back from spying out the land and ten of them say we can't do it and these two say we can
Then {{Samuel}} anoints {{David}}, and {{Jesse}} had seven other sons lined up, and he didn't even call {{David}} in from the field
{{Lydia}} was a seller of purple in Philippi, and she opens her house to {{Paul}} and {{Silas}}, and that's a house church in a woman's living room
turn with me to 1 {{Samuel}} 17, we're going to read about the valley of Elah, and I'll wait till the pages stop rustling

Then {{Jesus}} meets {{Peter}} on the beach and asks him three times do you love me. I think about [[Darrell]] on that, who messed up so bad and thought he was finished. And the Lord says feed my sheep.
{{Barnabas}} means son of encouragement and that's who he was, he took a chance on {{John Mark}} when {{Paul}} wouldn't
and {{Jesus}} says to the man at the pool, do you want to be well, and the man says Señor I have no one to put me in the water
{{Naaman}} was a mighty man but he was a leper, and he goes to {{Elisha}} and {{Elisha}} doesn't even come to the door
{{Job}} loses everything in one day, and his friends {{Eliphaz}} and {{Bildad}} and {{Zophar}} come and sit with him seven days, which was the best thing they did, and then they opened their mouths

{{Isaiah}} sees the Lord high and lifted up and says woe is me, and the seraph touches his lips with a coal. Now we have a young man in the youth group named [[Isaiah]] and I told him, you know you're named after a guy who got his lips burned, right?
{{Rebekah}} waters ten camels at the well. And [[Rebecca]] on the third row, I looked it up, it's the same name, so next work day you're hauling water.
{{John}} the Baptist is in prison and sends his disciples to ask {{Jesus}} are you the one or should we look for another
so {{Gideon}} has thirty-two thousand men and God says that's too many, send them home

{{Thomas}} wasn't there, and the others tell him we have seen the Lord, and he says unless I put my finger in the nail marks I will not believe, and {{Jesus}} comes back eight days later just for {{Thomas}}
{{Josiah}} was eight years old when he became king, eight, and he finds the book of the law in the temple and tears his clothes
{{Seth}} was born after {{Cain}} killed {{Abel}}, and {{Eve}} said God has appointed me another offspring. That's grief and hope in one sentence.

{{Joseph}} is just a carpenter, engaged, and he finds out {{Mary}} is pregnant. Now think about that conversation. And an angel tells him in a dream don't be afraid. And [[Joseph]] in our men's group, same name, would have needed more than a dream.
{{Moses}} stutters. He says Lord, send someone else. And God says who made the mouth? I thought of [[Denny]] last week when he said I'm no good at greeting.
{{Paul}} and {{Barnabas}} had a sharp disagreement in Acts 15. Sharp. They split up. And God used both. Sometimes that's [[Jim]] and [[Carl]] over the thermostat, and the Lord still uses them.
{{Peter}} walks on water, and for about three steps it works. Then he looks at the wind. And that's [[Cheryl]], who told me Thursday she looked at the bank balance.
The prodigal's older brother is standing outside the party. {{Jesus}} doesn't tell us if he went in. I think about my own brother [[Leon]] when I read that.

{{Naomi}} changes her name to {{Mara}}, which means bitter. And the women of Bethlehem take her back anyway. Our [[Naomi]], who sits on the left, said the same thing about herself last month, so women of this church, take her back.

{{Lazarus}} comes out of the tomb with the grave clothes still on, and {{Jesus}} says unbind him. That's the church's job. [[Hector]] has been out of prison six weeks and still has the grave clothes on, and we're the ones who unbind.

{{John Wesley}} was riding his horse through the English countryside, forty miles a day, preaching in fields because the Anglican churches shut their doors on him, and his brother {{Charles}} wrote the hymns
{{Augustine}} was bishop of Hippo in North Africa and his mother {{Monica}} prayed for him for seventeen years
In 1517 {{Martin Luther}} nailed ninety-five theses to a door in Wittenberg, or maybe he mailed them, historians argue about that
{{George Whitefield}} preached to crowds of thousands in Philadelphia and {{Benjamin Franklin}} walked off the distance to see how many could hear him
{{Lottie Moon}} went to China in 1873 and gave up her food so the Chinese children she served would have enough, and now every Christmas Southern Baptists give in her name
Our church was planted in 1911 by a circuit rider on a mule. Just last year [[Doris]] found his saddlebags in her barn, can you believe that, and they're in the glass case in the lobby.

{{Richard Allen}} walked out of St. George's Methodist in Philadelphia when they pulled him off his knees, and he founded the African Methodist Episcopal Church, Mother Bethel, and that's why many of us are here today
{{William Carey}}, the cobbler turned missionary to India, said expect great things from God, attempt great things for God
{{Polycarp}} was asked to curse Christ and he said eighty-six years I have served him and he has done me no wrong
{{Perpetua}} and {{Felicity}} were martyred in Carthage in the year 203, a young mother and her servant, and they sang in the arena
{{Jonathan Edwards}} preached Sinners in the Hands of an Angry God in Enfield and people grabbed the pillars of the church
{{Harriet Tubman}} used songs like Wade in the Water as signals, and our choir director Ms. [[Vernita]] found that in the archive at the museum last month
{{Sojourner Truth}} was born {{Isabella Baumfree}} and she picked her own name because she said the Spirit called her to travel and speak the truth
{{Dietrich Bonhoeffer}} came back from New York in 1939 even though he could have stayed safe, and he wrote that he had to live through this difficult time with the Christian people of Germany

The Azusa Street revival in Los Angeles in 1906 was led by {{William Seymour}}, a one-eyed Black preacher, son of former slaves, and it sparked Pentecostalism around the world, and folks in our church trace our roots right there
{{Charles Spurgeon}} preached at the Metropolitan Tabernacle in London to six thousand people every Sunday with no microphone
{{Fanny Crosby}} wrote about eight thousand hymns and she was blind from six weeks old, and she said she wouldn't want to be healed because the first face she wanted to see was the Savior's
{{Thomas Dorsey}} wrote Precious Lord Take My Hand after his wife {{Nettie}} died in childbirth, and that's a song that came out of a funeral
Count {{Zinzendorf}} and the Moravians had a prayer meeting in Herrnhut that went twenty-four hours a day for a hundred years

{{Francis Asbury}} rode a hundred thousand miles on horseback and owned almost nothing, a horse, a saddle and a Bible. And I think about [[Lyle]] who retired from the post office and still drives sixty miles to visit shut-ins.
{{Athanasius}} stood against the whole world over whether {{Jesus}} was truly God, at Nicaea in 325, and the emperor {{Constantine}} was right there in the room
{{Adoniram Judson}} spent seven years in Burma before his first convert, and his wife {{Ann}} smuggled food to him in prison in her hair

{{John Newton}} captained slave ships and one night in a storm he cried out to God, and years later he wrote Amazing Grace, and near the end he said I am a great sinner and {{Christ}} is a great Savior
{{Gladys Aylward}}, a London parlor maid, got to China on her own and walked a hundred children over the mountains
{{Samuel Ajayi Crowther}} was the first African Anglican bishop, a boy taken from his village in Yorubaland and sold, and he translated the Bible into Yoruba
{{Bartolome de las Casas}} spoke up for the native peoples of the Americas in the 1500s, a Spanish priest who changed his mind, and that's not nothing
{{Jim Elliot}} and four other men were killed in Ecuador in 1956, and then {{Elisabeth Elliot}} went back and lived among the same people who had killed her husband
{{Hudson Taylor}} wore Chinese clothes and braided his hair and the other missionaries thought he'd lost his mind
{{Martin Luther King}} said the church should be a thermostat and not a thermometer, it should set the temperature and not just report it
the Sandy Creek Baptists under {{Shubal Stearns}} shouted and fell out in the Carolina piedmont, and the old Presbyterians were horrified

{{Menno Simons}} was a Catholic priest in the Netherlands who became a leader of the Anabaptists, and that's where Mennonites get the name. We have a Mennonite family in our church, the [[Yoders]], who make the best apple butter you've ever had.
Mother {{Teresa}} said she was just a little pencil in God's hand, and she spent forty years in the slums of Calcutta
{{Thomas Aquinas}} had a vision near the end and said everything I have written seems like straw
Archbishop {{Desmond Tutu}} laughed his way through apartheid, and he said that goodness is stronger than evil

This building was dedicated in 1958 and the cornerstone has a Bible in it. Mr. [[Haskell]], who is ninety-three, was there as a boy and he told me the choir sang How Great Thou Art, which {{Stuart Hine}} had just translated.

{{William Wilberforce}} fought the slave trade for forty-six years and died three days after Parliament passed the Slavery Abolition Act. Forty-six years. [[Beverly]] asked me last week how long she should keep praying for her son, and I said ask {{Wilberforce}}.
{{Martin Luther}} was terrified of thunderstorms, and that's why he became a monk. And [[Frank]] in the back is nodding because he's scared of thunderstorms too and he's still a deacon.
{{John Wesley}}'s mother {{Susanna}} had nineteen children and still found an hour a day to pray. Mothers in this room, I see you. [[Carmen]], I'm looking at you, you have five.
In 1906 at Azusa Street {{William Seymour}} would put his head in a shoebox to pray. A shoebox. And our own Mother [[Lucille]] prayed in a closet for forty years, same thing.
{{Pandita Ramabai}} was an Indian Christian who opened homes for widows in the 1890s. A woman from Pune, [[Sunita]], who comes to our ESL class, told me her grandmother was raised in one.
The Council of Chalcedon met in 451 and said {{Christ}} is fully God and fully man. That's heavy. [[Dennis]] and I argued about it in the parking lot for an hour while the Pentecostals laughed.
{{Billy Sunday}} was a ballplayer before he was an evangelist, he played for the Chicago White Stockings. Coach [[Danny]] says that's the only conversion story he can relate to.
{{C. S. Lewis}} said that humility is not thinking less of yourself, it's thinking of yourself less
{{A. W. Tozer}} said what comes into our minds when we think about God is the most important thing about us
{{Tim Keller}} says the gospel is that you are more sinful and flawed than you ever dared believe and more loved and accepted than you ever dared hope
{{Dietrich Bonhoeffer}} called it cheap grace, grace without discipleship, and I wonder how many of us are on the cheap plan
{{Corrie ten Boom}} said never be afraid to trust an unknown future to a known God. And [[Linda]], you taped that on your fridge, I saw it in your kitchen, amen?
{{Martin Luther}} said I have so much to do today that I shall spend the first three hours in prayer
{{Elisabeth Elliot}} said do the next thing, and that's it, that's the whole sermon
{{Charles Spurgeon}} said by perseverance the snail reached the ark
{{Oswald Chambers}} wrote in My Utmost for His Highest that prayer does not fit us for the greater work, prayer is the greater work
as {{Maya Angelou}} said when people show you who they are believe them the first time
Dr. {{King}} said darkness cannot drive out darkness, only light can do that
Mr. {{Rogers}} said his mother told him look for the helpers, and this week I saw a lot of helpers, thank you [[Brenda]] and [[Cal]] for the casseroles

{{Lecrae}} has a line about being a mess and still being loved, and I think about that every time I'm in traffic

when {{Kirk Franklin}} came on the radio on the way here I turned it up, y'all, and [[Reggie]] in the passenger seat said Pastor, you're driving

{{Eugene Peterson}} called it a long obedience in the same direction

Saint {{Francis}} supposedly said preach the gospel at all times and use words if necessary, though he probably never said it
{{Billy Graham}} said it is the Holy Spirit who convicts, God who converts, and {{Jesus}} who saves, and I am just a witness
